about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Korean Doenjang Jjigae with Zucchini and Tofu
recipes.summary: A salty, earthy fermented soybean paste stew with zucchini, potato, tofu and chilli, served bubbling with rice.
steps: Bring the water to a simmer and whisk in the doenjang and gochugaru until the paste dissolves.
Add the potato and onion and simmer for 8 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Add the zucchini, tofu and garlic and simmer for 5 minutes, until the zucchini is soft.
Top with the spring onion and chilli and serve with the rice.
notes: Doenjang is salty, so taste before adding any extra salt.
Add a handful of sliced mushrooms if you like.

recipes.title: Korean Seolleongtang Ox Bone Soup
recipes.summary: A milky, mild beef bone broth with sliced brisket and noodles, seasoned at the table with salt, pepper and spring onion.
steps: Cover the bones and brisket with cold water, boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and meat.
Return them to the pot with the 3 litres water, onion, garlic and ginger and simmer gently for 2.5 hours, until the broth turns milky and the brisket is tender.
Lift out the brisket and slice it thinly, then strain the broth and discard the bones.
Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, until soft, then drain.
Divide the noodles, rice and brisket between bowls, ladle over the hot broth and top with the spring onion.
Season at the table with the salt and pepper.
notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until very tender and at least 70°C throughout, and keep the broth hot until serving.
Chill leftover broth quickly and use within 3 days.

recipes.title: Korean Galbitang Short Rib Soup
recipes.summary: A clear, savoury soup of tender beef short ribs, daikon and glass noodles, lightly sweet and deeply comforting.
steps: Boil the ribs in water for 8 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Return the ribs to the pot with 2 litres fresh water and simmer for 1 hour, skimming now and then.
Add the daikon, carrot, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar and simmer for 40 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, then add them to the soup for the final 3 minutes.
Beat the egg, pour a thin stream into the hot soup and stir once to make ribbons.
Top with the spring onion and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the ribs until very tender and at least 70°C throughout, and make sure the egg ribbons cook through in the simmering soup.
Skim off the fat once the soup has chilled.

recipes.title: Korean Dwaeji Gukbap Pork and Rice Soup
recipes.summary: A milky Busan pork and rice soup with garlic and spring onion, seasoned at the table with chilli.
steps: Cover the pork with water, boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse the pork.
Return it to the pot with 2 litres fresh water, onion, ginger, garlic and doenjang and simmer for 1 hour, until the pork is very tender.
Lift out the pork, slice it thinly and strain the broth.
Reheat the broth with the soy sauce and fish sauce until steaming hot.
Divide the rice and pork between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with spring onion, gochugaru and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until very tender and at least 70°C throughout.
Chill leftover soup within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

recipes.title: Korean Dakgomtang Chicken Soup
recipes.summary: A clean, milky whole-chicken soup with garlic, ginger and spring onion, seasoned with salt and pepper at the table.

items: 4 spring onions, 2 left whole and 2 sliced

steps: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic, ginger and the whole spring onions in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 50 minutes, skimming the surface, until the chicken is cooked through and falling from the bone.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard the skin and bones.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot and add the noodles, simmering for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken back and serve over the rice with sliced spring onion.
Season with the salt and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh and keep the soup hot until serving.
Chill leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

recipes.title: Korean Manduguk Dumpling Soup
recipes.summary: Plump pork and kimchi dumplings in a light soy and garlic broth with egg ribbons and seaweed.
steps: Mix the pork, kimchi, tofu, half the spring onion and half the garlic into a filling.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edges, fold into a parcel and press to seal.
Bring the stock, soy sauce and remaining garlic to a simmer until bubbling.
Add the dumplings and simmer for 6 minutes, until they float and the pork is cooked through.
Beat the eggs and pour them in a thin stream into the soup, stirring once until ribbons set.
Add the sesame oil and pepper, then ladle into bowls and top with the seaweed and remaining spring onion.
notes: Food safety: cook the dumplings until the pork reaches 75°C and no pink remains, and cook the egg until fully set.
Freeze uncooked dumplings on a tray, then bag them.

recipes.title: Korean Saengseon Guk White Fish and Daikon Soup
recipes.summary: A restorative morning soup of white fish simmered with daikon, sesame oil and egg, light and clean tasting.

items: 400g firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks

steps: Stir-fry the daikon in the sesame oil for 3 minutes, until it turns translucent.
Add the water and garlic and simmer for 10 minutes, until the daikon is soft.
Season with the soy sauce and fish sauce.
Add the fish and simmer for 4 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Beat the eggs and stir them into the soup in a thin stream until set.
Top with the spring onion and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and the egg until fully set.
Use any firm white fish.

recipes.title: Korean Mandu Dipping Sauce with Vinegar and Gochugaru
recipes.summary: A bright, sharp dumpling sauce of soy, rice vinegar, chilli flakes and sesame seeds.
steps: Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves.
Add the gochugaru, spring onion, sesame seeds and garlic.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with dumplings.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.
Serves 2 as a dip.

recipes.title: Japanese Oden Simmered Winter Hot Pot
recipes.summary: A gentle pot of daikon, boiled eggs, konnyaku and fish cakes simmered in a light dashi, served with hot mustard.

items: 1 daikon, about 400g, cut into thick rounds

steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel them.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide pot until the sugar dissolves.
Add the daikon and potatoes and simmer for 25 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the mushrooms, fish cakes, tofu and eggs and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until everything has taken on the flavour.
Serve in bowls with a little broth and a dab of mustard.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set and keep the pot hot until serving.
Oden is even better the next day.

recipes.title: Japanese Tara Chiri Cod Hot Pot
recipes.summary: A light kombu broth hot pot of cod, tofu, napa cabbage and mushrooms, dipped in soy and lemon at the table.
steps: Put the water and kombu in a wide pot and heat gently to just below a simmer until small bubbles form, then remove the kombu.
Add the carrot, cabbage stalks and mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cod, tofu, leek and cabbage leaves and simmer for 6 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flaking.
Serve straight from the pot with the soy and lemon dipping sauce and spring onion for dipping.
Finish with the leftover broth and rice if you like.
notes: Food safety: cook the cod until opaque throughout and flaking.
Do not leave the pot sitting warm for hours.

recipes.title: Japanese Asari Clam Miso Soup
recipes.summary: Sweet little clams opening in a savoury miso broth, finished with spring onion.

items: 800g small clams, purged in salted water

steps: Scrub the clams and rinse them well.
Warm the water and kombu in a pot, then discard the kombu just before it boils.
Add the clams and sake and cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, until they open.
Remove from the heat and whisk in the miso, discarding any clams that stay shut.
Top with the spring onion and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook until the clams open and the flesh is opaque, and discard any clams that are open before cooking or that do not open after cooking.
Do not boil the miso, which dulls the flavour.

recipes.title: Japanese Gyoza Dipping Sauce with Rayu
recipes.summary: A classic gyoza sauce of soy, rice vinegar and chilli oil with a little sesame and ginger.
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, chilli oil and sesame oil in a small bowl until combined.
Stir in the ginger and spring onion.
Serve alongside pan-fried gyoza.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week.
Add more rayu for extra heat.

recipes.title: Japanese Kimchi Nabe
recipes.summary: A fiery kimchi hot pot with pork, tofu, mushrooms and leeks, finished with rice or noodles in the leftover broth.
steps: Bring the stock, kimchi, kimchi juice and gochujang to a simmer in a wide pot until bubbling.
Add the pork and cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the tofu, mushrooms and soy sauce and simmer for 5 minutes, until the pork is cooked through.
Top with the spring onion and serve with the rice.
Add noodles to the remaining broth to finish.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until no pink remains and it reaches 70°C.
The kimchi brings plenty of salt, so taste before adding more.

recipes.title: Japanese Tamago Tofu Clear Soup
recipes.summary: Silky chilled egg tofu cubes set in a delicate hot dashi with mushroom and spring onion.

items: 300ml dashi stock, for the egg tofu

steps: Whisk the eggs gently with the 300ml dashi, the 1 tsp mirin and the salt, avoiding bubbles, then strain into a small lined tin.
Cover with foil and steam over simmering water for 18 minutes, until just set, then chill for at least 1 hour.
Simmer the 800ml dashi with the soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin and mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Cut the egg tofu into cubes and place in bowls.
Ladle the hot soup over and top with spring onion and peel.
notes: Food safety: steam the egg tofu until fully set and keep it chilled until serving.
Serve within 2 days.

recipes.title: Thai Tom Yum Goong Prawn Soup
recipes.summary: A hot and sour prawn soup with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaf, mushrooms and a good squeeze of lime.
steps: Simmer the stock, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chillies for 8 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and chilli jam, then taste and adjust.
Scatter over the coriander and serve at once.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque throughout.
Do not eat the lemongrass, galangal or lime leaves.

recipes.title: Thai Gaeng Jued Woonsen Glass Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: A mild, clear Thai soup of glass noodles, minced pork, tofu and cabbage, gently seasoned with garlic and white pepper.
steps: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, then drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Bring the stock and garlic to a simmer until bubbling.
Roll the pork into small balls and drop them in, simmering for 5 minutes.
Add the carrot, tofu and cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the noodles, fish sauce and pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Top with the spring onion and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork balls until they reach 75°C and no pink remains.
Add a splash of soy sauce for more depth.

recipes.title: Thai Gaeng Liang Pumpkin and Prawn Soup
recipes.summary: A peppery, herbal Thai soup of pumpkin, sweet corn and prawns thickened with a spoon of shrimp paste and shallots.
steps: Grind or blend the curry paste, shrimp paste and shallots into a rough paste.
Bring the water to the boil until bubbling and stir in the paste until dissolved.
Add the pumpkin and corn and simmer for 10 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink.
Stir in the fish sauce, pepper and basil.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque throughout.
Add chilli for more heat.

recipes.title: Thai Tom Saap Isaan Pork Rib Soup
recipes.summary: A sour, spicy Isaan soup of tender pork ribs with lemongrass, galangal, chilli and lime.

items: 800g pork spare ribs, cut into short pieces

steps: Boil the ribs in water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Return them to the pot with 1.5 litres fresh water, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, dried chillies and shallots.
Simmer gently for 1 hour, until the pork is tender.
Season with the fish sauce and lime juice.
Top with the herbs and spring onion.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until very tender, at least 70°C throughout.
Skim the surface while simmering for a cleaner broth.

recipes.title: Thai Gaeng Hed Mushroom Jungle Soup
recipes.summary: A clear, fiery northern Thai soup of mixed mushrooms, long beans, lemongrass and Thai basil without coconut milk.

items: 150g long beans, cut into short lengths

steps: Simmer the stock, curry paste, lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes.
Add the eggplant and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and beans and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender.
Season with the soy sauce and sugar.
Stir in the basil before serving.
notes: Add chilli slices for extra heat.
Serve with jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Lao Or Lam Stew
recipes.summary: A herbal Lao pork stew of eggplant, mushrooms and long beans thickened with toasted sticky rice.
steps: Simmer the pork, water, lemongrass, shallots and dried chillies for 30 minutes, until the pork is almost tender.
Add the eggplant, mushrooms and beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice powder and simmer for 5 minutes, until the stew thickens.
Season with the fish sauce and stir in the dill and basil.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork until tender and at least 70°C throughout.
Make the rice powder by toasting sticky rice in a dry pan until golden, then grinding it.

recipes.title: Lao Jeow Mak Len Roasted Tomato Dip
recipes.summary: A smoky Lao tomato dip of charred tomatoes, chilli, garlic and shallot, pounded into a rustic relish for sticky rice.
steps: Roast the tomatoes, garlic, shallots and chillies under a hot grill or in a dry pan for 12 minutes, turning, until blackened in patches.
Peel the garlic and shallots.
Grind the chillies, garlic and shallots into a paste, then add the tomatoes and crush roughly.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, spring onion and coriander.
notes: Serve with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Lao Khao Piak Sen Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: A comforting Lao noodle soup of chewy rice noodles in clear chicken broth with garlic oil and herbs.
steps: Simmer the stock, chicken and ginger for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 2 minutes, until golden.
Cook the noodles in the stock for 5 minutes, until tender.
Season with the fish sauce.
Serve the noodles and broth with the chicken, garlic oil, spring onion, coriander, chilli and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C throughout and keep the soup hot until serving.
Rice noodles are best eaten straight away.

recipes.title: Lao Tam Mak Hoong Papaya Salad
recipes.summary: Shredded green papaya pounded with chilli, garlic, fermented fish sauce and lime for a funky, fiery Lao salad.

items: 100g long beans, cut into short lengths

steps: Crush the garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar.
Add the long beans and bruise lightly.
Add the papaya, tomato, fish sauce, lime juice and palm sugar and toss, crushing gently, until the papaya softens.
Taste and adjust for sour, salty and hot.
Scatter over the peanuts and serve at once.
notes: Serve immediately with sticky rice.
Padaek is very pungent, so use fish sauce if you want it milder.

recipes.title: Lao Jeow Bong Chilli Paste
recipes.summary: A sweet-savoury Lao chilli paste of dried chillies, galangal, shallot and garlic, slowly cooked in oil.
steps: Soak the chillies in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Dry-fry the shallots, garlic and galangal for 6 minutes, until golden.
Blend the chillies with the shallots, garlic and galangal into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 8 minutes over low heat, until darkened and fragrant.
Stir in the tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and sesame seeds.
notes: Keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for 2 weeks.
Eat with sticky rice and grilled vegetables.
